title: S013 — Future observability / minimal sufficient retention
description: S012 left a conservative FoldStateDelta that over-retains (category C: fold-changed but apparently future-irrelevant). S013 asks whether Somnium can distinguish fold-changed-AND-future-relevant from fold-changed-BUT-future-irrelevant without a second semantic authority, using an observational definition of future relevance: I is future-observable within H iff there exists a suffix S with derive(H+S) != derive(H without I + S).
result_summary: HOLD. The suffix oracle OVERTURNS S012's reading of category C. S012 classified C by immediate removal only; under suffix exploration almost every fold-changed step is future-observable. Full run: verrin A=124 B=16 C=0 D=20; ordos A=119 B=21 C=1 D=19. Of 281 fold-changed steps, only 17 were future-invisible within the tested suffix bound; 37 were semantic-invisible but future-visible (the S010 class). Smallest exposing suffix is the S010 shape: I=forceEvent(ev/maren-return), S=[negateEvent(ev/maren-return)]. No generic rule expressible from fold information separates the 17 invisible steps from the 264 relevant ones without semantic interpretation, so a tighter retention rule is NOT justified; S012's conservative boundary is close to necessary, not merely safe. S012 delta-retention re-run: 16/16 differential equivalent. Semantic authority remained singular (the oracle only calls derive; no semantic rule encoded).
key_distinctions: fold-state change, semantic-state change and future relevance are three distinct dimensions (confirmed).
S012's category C was largely 'not relevant immediately', not 'truly irrelevant'.
17/281 fold-changed steps were future-invisible under the tested bound; 'not observed' != 'proven irrelevant'.

Branch semantics: the same forceEvent target is future-invisible in one history and observable in another, so relevance must not key on intervention identity alone (S012's per-step delta already satisfies this).
recommendation: Keep S012's conservative FoldStateDelta boundary. Do not pursue a tighter retention rule. If anything is productionized, it is S012's mechanism as-is (experimental API), with the honest statement that it may over-retain a small, unidentifiable minority.
limitations: The suffix population is finite; 'not observed' != 'proven irrelevant'.
S013's corpus is smaller than S012's (suffix search is expensive), so A/B/C/D counts are not directly comparable to S012's.
Horizons beyond H=20 per history were not fully suffix-searched; H=100000 was not practical for the oracle.
No claim of global minimality; no canonicality attempt.
references: S012 report / req-012; S011 report / req-011
